newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MARSEILLE SEEK QUICK DOUBLE OVER AUXERRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MARSEILLE SEEK QUICK DOUBLE OVER AUXERRE.

text.p: Marseille will be looking to complete a double in one week over Auxerre when they entertain the French champions in the first division on Sunday.
The 1993 European Cup winners, back in the top flight after two seasons in division two, beat Auxerre 3-2 in the second round of the League Cup at the Velodrome on Tuesday.
But Marseille midfielder Eric Roy warned the task was only half complete.
"We're only at halftime, the counter is back to zero, we have another match to come," he said.
Marseille, having overcome early-season doldrums, have gone seven games unbeaten including the League Cup victory and are in confident mood.
"Auxerre are always interesting rivals. They're one of the best teams in Europe. This gives us the possibility of finding exactly where we stand," said Marseille coach Gerard Gili.
Auxerre are fourth, seven points behind joint leaders Monaco and Paris Saint-Germain. Marseille are 13th.
"The duels (between the players) that we won were the key to our success in the League Cup. We shook them physically and upset their marking," Gili said.
But Gili will be well aware of the capacity of his astute Auxerre couterpart Guy Roux to learn from his side's mistakes on Tuesday and make the necessary alterations.
Roux will also be able to include key players who missed the League Cup clash through injury, such as Algerian international Moussa Saib.
"It was important to win the first hand. That surely has affected them," said France midfielder Reynald Pedros, who scored his first goal for Marseille on Tuesday since joining them from Nantes.

"It's a small psychological advantage for OM (Olympique Marseille)," added veteran midfielder Jean-Philippe Durand, the only remaining link with Marseille's European Cup-winning side, who is doubtful for Sunday with a knee injury.

If Durand fails a late fitness test his place will be taken by Bulgaria's Yordan Lechkov, who had lost favour with Gili and was consigned to the bench in recent league matches, but had a very good game on Tuesday at the hub of Marseille's attacks.
"After three days of rest I still feel quite a bit of pain. That's doesn't make me very optimistic," said Marseille captain Durand.
Germany goalkeeper Andreas Koepke will be back in time for the match after playing for his country in a World Cup qualifier on Saturday.
Striker Xavier Graveliane, Marseille's top scorer with five goals, should also be back in the side after a one-match suspension.
Auxerre, however, may be unable to count on their striker Lilian Laslandes, vital as a targetman, who came off injured after less than an hour on Tuesday.
If Laslanedes is unavailable, Thomas Deniaud will stand in at the front of the attack to link up with wing Steve Marlet, who scored both Auxerre's goals in the League Cup match.
The injury woes that have plagued Auxerre this season could also deprive Roux of defender Alain Goma, who missed Tuesday's game.
Roux, whose side are European Cup quarter-finalists, said: "We mustn't forget that it was our 28th match this season and legs are beginning to get very heavy."
Probable teams:

Marseille - Andreas Koepke; Hamada Jambay, Alberto Malusci, Ivan Franceschini; Eric Roy, Jean-Philippe Durand or Yordan Lechkov, Ludovic Asuar, Olivier Echouafni, Reynald Pedros; Marc Libbra, Xavier Gravelaine.
Auxerre - Fabien Cool; Alain Goma, Frederic Danjou, Franck Silvestre, Franck Rabarivony; Abdelhajid Tasfaout, Philippe Violeau, Eric Assati, Moussa Saib; Steve Marlet, Lilian Laslandes.
